content: The immunoglobulin lambda locus, abbreviated as IGL@, is a specific region located on human chromosome 22. This locus contains the genes responsible for encoding the lambda light chains of antibodies, also known as immunoglobulins. Immunoglobulins are essential components of the immune system. They recognize foreign antigens and trigger immune responses, such as phagocytosis and activation of the complement system. Each immunoglobulin molecule is composed of two identical heavy chains and two identical light chains. The light chains are classified into two types: kappa and lambda. The IGL@ locus represents the germline organization of the lambda light chain genes and includes variable (V), joining (J), and constant (C) gene segments. During B cell development, a recombination event at the DNA level joins a single V segment with a J segment. Subsequently, the C segment is joined at the RNA level through splicing. The recombination of various V segments with multiple J segments generates a broad diversity of antigen recognition. Additional diversity is introduced through junctional diversity, which involves the random addition of nucleotides by the enzyme terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase, and somatic hypermutation, which occurs during B cell maturation in the spleen and lymph nodes. Some V segments and three C segments within the locus are incapable of encoding functional proteins and are classified as pseudogenes. Additionally, the locus contains several non-immunoglobulin genes, many of which are either pseudogenes or predicted based on computational analysis or homology with other species. The immunoglobulin lambda locus includes the following genes: 1. IGLC@ (constant group): IGLC1: Immunoglobulin lambda constant 1 (Mcg marker) IGLC2: Immunoglobulin lambda constant 2 (Kern-Ozmarker) IGLC3: Immunoglobulin lambda constant 3 (Kern-Oz+ marker) IGLC7: Immunoglobulin lambda constant 7 2. IGLJ@ (joining group): IGLJ1, IGLJ2, IGLJ3, IGLJ6, IGLJ7: Immunoglobulin lambda joining segments 3. IGLV@ (variable group): IGLV1-36, IGLV1-40, IGLV1-44, IGLV1-47, IGLV1-51, IGLV1-62 IGLV2-5, IGLV2-8, IGLV2-11, IGLV2-14, IGLV2-18, IGLV2-23 IGLV3-1, IGLV3-10, IGLV3-12, IGLV3-16, IGLV3-19, IGLV3-21, IGLV3-25, IGLV3-27 IGLV4-3, IGLV4-60, IGLV4-69 IGLV5-37, IGLV5-39, IGLV5-45, IGLV5-52 IGLV6-57 IGLV7-43 IGLV9-49 IGLV10-54 The protein encoded by the IGLC2 gene is known as the immunoglobulin lambda chain C region. This protein plays a critical role in the structure and function of immunoglobulins in humans.
